insights.summary: FY26 revenue grew 35.6% to ₹4,221 Cr with EBITDA up 124% to ₹579 Cr (13.7%) and adjusted PAT of ₹368 Cr; Q4 alone was ₹1,422 Cr at an 18% EBITDA margin. STQC rules pushed out Chinese brands and CP PLUS's market share rose from about 30% to about 45%. Management raised FY27 guidance to ₹6,000-6,500 Cr revenue (about 50% growth), 14-15% EBITDA and 8.5-9.5% PAT, with growth split between 25-30% volume and a 20-25% rise in average prices as memory and chip costs climb.

what_changed.text: FY27 guidance raised to ₹6,000-6,500 Cr revenue, 14-15% EBITDA, 8.5-9.5% PAT
Market share about 45% (Q3 FY26) vs 36% projected at IPO
Partnerships with Qualcomm (AI cameras) and L&T Semiconductor (9 million cameras over three years); cable JV with Orient Cables
Price rises of a few points every month to pass on memory and chip inflation

tone.label: confident
tone.quote: We remain confident, optimistic, and committed to building a stronger, more innovative, and future-ready organization.

analyst_questions.answer: A mix of low-cost inventory, the Q4 price rise and more high-end STQC-certified project SKUs; low-cost inventory is now used up.
DDR3 supply is shrinking as makers move to AI memory; scale lets CP PLUS secure supply ahead of smaller rivals.
Yes for FY27 and FY28, from localisation, premium mix and enterprise business; Q4 was a one-off.
Cycle rose as creditors fell with advance payments to secure chips; funded from internal accruals and some debt.

red_flags.text: Q4 FY26 margins were flattered by low-cost inventory that has now run out.
Component costs expected to keep rising until 2027; some supply contracts are being voided under force majeure.
Almost half of the guided growth is price (20-25% ASP rise), not volume.
Cash conversion cycle rising as the company pays suppliers in advance.

EBITDA margin holding 14-15% without cheap inventory
Housing plant Phase 1 by Q2 FY27
Competition as more brands get STQC certified

business_snapshot.what_they_make: Video surveillance: CP PLUS cameras (IP and HD analog), recorders, AI analytics; manufactured at Kadapa (2.5 million units a month), plus distribution of other brands
business_snapshot.customers: Distributors and dealers, system integrators, enterprises, government (15-20% of revenue) and homes
business_snapshot.revenue_mix: CP PLUS 86% of revenue, IP products 73% of CP PLUS; mostly domestic
business_snapshot.demand_drivers: STQC rules favouring Indian brands, IP upgrades, smart cities and AI video analytics
